brief:
- first paragraph of the section; the heading has just said "Make a Simple Vow"
- the guide: "When promises still carry some credibility, a quiet vow can help." In plain words: if your promises still mean something to your little one, a quiet vow can help. (Not Every Hero Wears A Cape already said your little one may have had grown-ups who said sweet things and then did nothing, and that you may have done it too.)
- the guide: "If the present adult still intends to frighten, exploit, or harm vulnerability, skip the vow and the child-contact exercise; work first on adult choice and non-harm." The article already has a whole section on this, "When the Present-Day Adult Is Dangerous to the Child", which ends with the little one staying out of it until scaring somebody has stopped sounding fun. Point back to it in a few words: if that section was about you, the vow waits, and the grown-up comes first. Word it so an ordinary reader doesn't start wondering whether they're the dangerous one.
- the guide: "Otherwise, you can make it with or without a visualization of the two of you playing on a swing:" You can say it with or without picturing the two of you on a swing. End leading into the vow (a colon is fine); the vow itself is the next paragraph.
length: two to three sentences, 35 to 70 words
guide_passage: When promises still carry some credibility, a quiet vow can help. If the present adult still intends to frighten, exploit, or harm vulnerability, skip the vow and the child-contact exercise; work first on adult choice and non-harm. Otherwise, you can make it with or without a visualization of the two of you playing on a swing:
next: “I know you are in there. I love you.* You do not have to love me back or trust me yet. I cannot promise that nothing painful will happen, that I will always know what to do, or that I will never react badly. I can promise to tell you the truth, listen when you are angry, make our life safer where I can, take the next protective step I can see, and come back to repair when I fail. You do not have to believe these words. Watch what I do.”
